Theorem
[Dirichlet problem for uniformly elliptic equations in dimension two] 1. ch12:12.5\group chapter-12Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0317 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^2$ satisfy an exterior sphere condition and let $\varphi \in C^0(\partial \Omega )$. If $Q$ satisfies (i)--(iii), then egin{equation} ag {12.29} Qu=0\quad ext{in }\Omega , \qquad u=\varphi \quad ext{on }\partial \Omega \end{equation} has a solution $u\in C^{2, eta }(\Omega )\cap C^0(\overline\Omega )$.
Proof

\sketch First replace (12.27) by

egin{equation} ag {12.30} |f|/\lambda \le \mu <\infty . \end{equation}

For $v$ in a bounded subset of a weighted $C^{1,\alpha }$ space, freeze the coefficients at $(v,Dv)$ and solve

egin{equation} ag {12.31} ar a u_{xx}+2 ar b u_{xy}+ ar c u_{yy}+ ar f=0 \quad ext{in }\Omega , \qquad u=\varphi \quad ext{on }\partial \Omega . \end{equation}

The maximum principle gives $|u|_0\le \sup _{\partial \Omega }|\varphi |+C\mu =:M_0$, and Theorem 21 gives

egin{equation} ag {12.32} |u|^*_{1,\alpha } \le C\left(|u|_0+\mu (\operatorname {diam}\Omega )^2 ight) \le K, \qquad \alpha =\alpha (\gamma (M_0)). \end{equation}

Define the convex set

\[ \mathcal G=\{ v:|v|^*_{1,\alpha }\le K,\ |v|_0\le M_0\} \]

and let $Tv$ be the solution of (12.31). Exterior-sphere barriers give, uniformly in $v$,

egin{equation} ag {12.33} |Tv(z)-\varphi (z_0)| \le \varepsilon +k_\varepsilon w(z) \qquad (z_0\in \partial \Omega ). \end{equation}

Thus $T\mathcal G$ is precompact in the weaker weighted $C^1$ norm. Interior Schauder compactness, (12.33), and uniqueness make $T$ continuous, so the Schauder fixed-point theorem gives a solution under (12.30).

For the general case divide by $\lambda $ and rewrite (12.27)–(12.28) as

egin{equation} |f|\le \mu (|u|)(1+|p|+|q|). ag {12.34} \end{equation}

egin{equation} f\operatorname {sign}u\le u (1+|p|+|q|). ag {12.35} \end{equation}

Let $\psi _N(t)=t$ for $|t|\le N$ and $\psi _N(t)=N\operatorname {sign}t$ otherwise, and truncate $f$ in all three variables $u,p,q$. Solve

egin{equation} ag {12.36} egin{aligned} Q_Nu={}& a(x,y,u,Du)u_{xx}+2b(x,y,u,Du)u_{xy}\ & +c(x,y,u,Du)u_{yy}+f_N(x,y,u,Du)=0, \qquad u=\varphi ext{ on }\partial \Omega . \end{aligned} \end{equation}

The sign condition gives the $N$-independent bound

egin{equation} ag {12.37} \sup _\Omega |u_N| \le \sup _{\partial \Omega }|\varphi | +C_1( u ,\operatorname {diam}\Omega )=:M. \end{equation}

The gradient estimate first gives

egin{equation} ag {12.38} [u_N]^*_{1,\alpha } \le C\left(|u_N|_0+|f_N|_0^{(2)} ight), \end{equation}

and then, using (12.34) and interpolation,

egin{equation} ag {12.39} |u_N|^*_{1,\alpha } \le C(M,\gamma (M),\mu (M),\operatorname {diam}\Omega ). \end{equation}

Interior Schauder compactness supplies a subsequential solution of $Qu=0$; the same uniform barriers as in (12.33) pass the boundary values to the limit.

□

If $\partial \Omega $ and $\varphi $ are in $C^{2, eta }$ and $a,b,c,f\in C^ eta (\overline\Omega imes \mathbb R imes \mathbb R^2)$, the solution is in $C^{2, eta }(\overline\Omega )$. Condition (12.28) may be dropped when a uniform zeroth-order bound is otherwise known, and (12.27) may be dropped when a uniform gradient bound is known. The exterior sphere condition may be replaced by any hypothesis providing the uniform linear barriers, including an exterior cone condition.
